questions.question: Who is the chairman of NITI Aayog?
questions.solution:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the chairman of NITI Aayog.

 
• The first meeting of NITI Aayog was chaired by Narendra Modi on 8 February 2015.
 
• It was established with the aim to achieve sustainable development goals.
 
• It also helps to enhance cooperative federalism by fostering the involvement of State Governments of India.

questions.question: Which of the following is related to oilseed production?
questions.solution:
__**Yellow revolution**__ is related to oilseed production.

 
• It was established for ensuring optimum utilization of production, processing, management and technology in oilseed crops.
 
• The term Yellow Revolution stands for the People Power Revolution in the Philippines in 1986 against President Ferdinand Marcos.

questions.question: According to Hindu calendar, the Indian Constitution came into force on?
questions.solution:
The Indian Constitution came into force on Margsheersh Shukla Saptami, Samvat 2006 Vikrami.

 
• As per the English calendar, it came into force on 26th January 1950.
 
• It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949.

questions.question: What does the term "Fourth estate" refer to?
questions.solution:
The term **"Fourth estate"** refers to** Press.**

 
• It is called the fourth estate in the United States because they observe the political process of democratization as they contribute to mass media.
 
• There were three estates namely- the clergy, the nobility, and the third estate the commoners.
 
• The fourth estate is the press and was established in **1837.**
 
• It is also called the fourth branch of government.

questions.question: The script of Indus Valley Civilization is/was ________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is still undeciphered**__

__
 
• The script of **Indus Valley Civilization**__ is still __**undeciphered**__.
 
• There are too many uncertainties in the Indus script.
 
• Many people said that it is pictorial in nature, alphabetic in nature, and phonetic as well.
 
• The writing style visible to be from the right to the left in many places.
 
• Hence, there is no concrete evidence to suggest that any of the scripts that are currently used in the Indian subcontinent have developed from the Indus script.

questions.question: Who installed the "bell of justice"?
questions.solution:
• **Jahangir **installed the "bell of justice".
 
• When he was emperor, he received complaints that Mughal soldiers were kidnapping the women of defeated kingdoms, then he decided to put a bell that is known as the bell of Justice.
 
• Therefore soldiers would observe the number of times the bell struck and punished them accordingly.

questions.question: What percentage of the Earth's area is approximately ﬁlled with water?
questions.solution:
Approximately 70% of the Earth's area is approximately ﬁlled with water.

 
• While the other 30% consists of continents and islands.
 
• As per studies, the amount of water that exists as groundwater, rivers, lakes, and streams would be just over 10.6 million km3.

questions.question: Chambal River is the tributary of which of the following river?
questions.solution:
The Chambal River is the tributary of **Yamuna **River.

 
• It rises in the Vindhyachal range South of Mhow, the western state of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows from the north into a southeastern state of Rajasthan.
 
• It ends on the confluence of five rivers which includes the Chambal, Kwari, Yamuna, Sind, Pahuj, at Pachnada near Bhareh in Uttar Pradesh, at the border of Bhind and Etawah districts.

questions.question: Which one of the following items is not a source of Vitamin C?
questions.solution:
The egg is not the source of Vitamin c.

 
• Eggs contain the protein and fat with the exception of vitamin C.
 
• Eggs also contain natural Vitamin D.
 
• 
 
Vitamin C, also known as ascorbic acid, is an essential nutrient that plays a critical role in various bodily functions, such as the synthesis of collagen, iron absorption, and maintenance of the immune system.

 

Here are several primary dietary sources of Vitamin C:-

 
• **Citrus Fruits:** Oranges, grapefruits, lemons, and limes are among the highest sources of Vitamin C.
 
• **Berries: **Strawberries, raspberries, blueberries, and cranberries are also high in Vitamin C.
 
• **Tropical Fruits**: Kiwi, guava, papaya, pineapple, and particularly mangos and acerola cherries have abundant Vitamin C.
 
• **Vegetables:** Bell peppers (especially red bell peppers), broccoli, Brussels sprouts, and leafy greens like spinach and kale have high Vitamin C. Cabbage, especially red cabbage, also has a good amount.
 
• **Other Fruits**: Tomatoes, cherries, and melons (like cantaloupe) provide Vitamin C.
 
• **Herbs:** Fresh herbs such as parsley and thyme have substantial amounts of Vitamin C.
 
• **Potatoes: **Both sweet potatoes and regular potatoes have some amount of Vitamin C.

questions.question: What is the normal temperature of the human body?
questions.solution:
The normal temperature of the human body is 37°C or 98.6°F.

 
• A temperature over 100.4°F (38°C) is considered as fever which is caused by an infection or illness.
 
• The body temperature also varies by person, age, activity and time of day.

questions.question: Iodization of Salt is a public health measure to prevent _______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Iodization of Salt is a public health measure to **prevent goitre.**__
 
• Lack of dietary iodine is the main cause of **goitre disease.**
 
• Goitre also occurs when the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone.

questions.question: A light year is a unit of which of the following?
questions.solution:
A light year is a unit of distance.

 
• It is a distance that can travel in a year.
 
• It is a unit of distance, in terms of time.

 
• Hence, one Light year = 1 year time × speed of light = (365.4 ×24×60×60) seconds × (3×10⁸) m/s. = 9.461×10^15 metres.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an input device?
questions.solution:
The __**microprocessor**__ is not an input device. It is an **output device**.

 
• A microprocessor is an integrated circuit that incorporates core functions of a computer’s central processing unit.
 
• It is a programmable multipurpose silicon chip that accepts binary data as input and provides output after processing it as per the instructions stored in the memory.
 
• **Mouse, keyboard, and Joystick** are the **input devices**.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is used for artiﬁcial ripening of green fruits?
questions.solution:
__**Acetylene**__ gas is used for artiﬁcial ripening of green fruits.

 
• It is produced when artificial ripening agent calcium carbide comes in contact with moisture.
 
• It has carcinogenic properties. Its compound formula is C₂H2.
 
• It is also used in the steel plants for the purpose of welding and cutting.

questions.question: Which of the following living beings is most likely to produce greenhouse gases?
questions.solution:
Green plants are most likely to produce greenhouse gases.

 
• Greenhouse gases consists of gases such as carbon dioxide, methane, water vapor, nitrous oxide, and ozone.
 
• These gases absorb heat which produced from the Sun.
 
• Bacteria, Fungi, and Earthworm do not produce greenhouse gases. However, from recent studies, it has been confirmed that some of the green plants release greenhouse gases.

questions.solution:
Madhu Kishwar does not belong to Madhubani Painting.

• She was also a professor at the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies as well as the Director of the Indic Studies Project.
 
• Their main aims to promote the study of "Religions and Cultures in the Indic Civilization".

**Madhubani Painting:**

 
• Madhubani art (also Mithila art) is a style of painting practiced in the Mithila region of India and Nepal.
 
• It is named after the Madhubani district of Bihar, India, which is where it originated.
 
• Artists create these paintings using a variety of mediums, including their own fingers, or twigs, brushes, nib-pens, and matchsticks.
 
• The paint is created using natural dyes and pigments. The paintings are characterised by their eye-catching geometrical patterns. There is ritual content for particular occasions, such as birth or marriage, and festivals, such as Holi, Surya Shasti, Kali Puja, Upanayana, and Durga Puja.
